Subject: Post-call: Prompt/log ingestion plan & POC success criteria (Brightline)

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Below is a concise recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the POC kickoff. Please flag anything I missed.

High level goal
- Validate Redwood inference quality & latency on Brightline clinical triage prompts and recent production logs; measure throughput cost and regression risk for shorter sequences (~50 tokens) and longer guided responses (~400 tokens).

Success criteria (proposal)
1) Quality: >=90% pass rate on your internal QA rubric across 3 prompt buckets (short, medium, long) using the prompt set you provide.
2) Latency: median token latency <= 18ms/token at 8 concurrent sessions; p95 <= 45ms/token on our dedicated config.
3) Cost: token cost reduction <= 20% vs baseline (your current endpoint) using recommended quantization/batching.
4) No PII leakage flagged in 1 week of automated checks on the ingested logs.

Deliverables Redwood will provide
- Eval harness + scoreboard with per-prompt metrics.
- Inference config recommendations (batching, quant, KV cache policy).
- Runbook for reproducing results and a handoff deck.

What we need from Brightline (next 2 weeks)
- Representative prompt set + 2k anonymized request/response pairs (CSV) across buckets. See sample schema attached. (Simon/Priya)
- S3 write access or signed URL to upload: s3://brightline-poc-uploads/prompts/ (we can accept Drive link if preferred).
- Point of contact for QA rubric and acceptance decision: name + role + availability.

Proposed timeline
- Day 0 (today): intake alignment (this thread)
- Day 2-5: customer uploads prompts/logs; Redwood confirms receipt and runs quick sanity checks
- Day 6-10: initial eval runs, we share preliminary scoreboard and config tweaks
- Day 11-14: refinement run + final report and handoff

Owners
- Redwood: Rachel Kim (technical lead, evaluation), Ben Carter (solutions engineer, infra & S3 ingest), Neha Kapoor (customer success, acceptance coordination)
- Brightline: Simon Wu (product), Priya Patel (clinical QA)

Attachments: brightline_sample_prompts.csv, redwood_poc_success_criteria_v1.pdf, s3-transfer-instructions.txt

Thanks — I’ll check back on Friday if we haven’t received the upload.

—
Rachel Kim

Priya — quick answers from infra & security perspective.

PII detection: we run a two-stage pipeline for POC ingests:
- Stage 1 (rule-based): high-confidence regex detectors for SSN, credit card formats, phone numbers, date-of-birth patterns.
- Stage 2 (model-assisted): a lightweight classifier tuned for PHI/PII entity presence (names, addresses, medical terms) — flagged items are surfaced in a quarantine report.

Retention & deletion: Redwood will: 
- Retain raw uploaded artifacts in a customer-scoped S3 area for the duration of the POC (default 30 days).
- Perform automatic deletion on day 31 unless you request extended retention (we record requests in the intake doc).
- Provide a deletion proof file (sha256 + timestamp) once deletion completes.

Security posture: all uploads happen into a customer-owned S3 bucket (your account); we only request a write-only IAM role scoped to a prefix. If you prefer, we can accept an encrypted transfer link (pre-signed URL) instead.

Next steps checklist
- Simon: confirm when infra will share the write-only role/credentials (expect 24h).
- Priya: confirm rubric sync slot (Rachel will send a calendar invite for 6/28 10:30am PT unless you suggest otherwise).
- Brightline: upload sample CSV to s3://brightline-poc-uploads/prompts/ and notify this thread.

We’ll stand up the eval harness as soon as ingestion completes and share an initial scoreboard within 72 hours of receipt.

—
